force.title: The Fractional Worker
force.signature: Permanent jobs unbundle into gigs, fractional roles, and expert networks — the firm rents talent by the hour, and the platform in the middle takes the cut.

A \u00b7 Renting the expert: Companies rent senior judgment by the call or the project instead of hiring it full-time.
Fractional CFOs, CMOs, and coaches replace full-time executives at smaller firms.
Whole functions — HR, marketing, compliance — get rented from consultants instead of staffed.
B \u00b7 The platforms in the middle: Recruiters and brokers monetize the matching as work fragments.
Short-course and certification providers sell the fast credentials the gig market rewards.
C \u00b7 The tensions: Fractional work shifts benefits and stability onto the worker; insurers reprice the risk.
Professional firms lean on contractors and offshoring, thinning the permanent core.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: the unit of work shrinks from the job to the task; platforms and specialists win, stability loses.
